guidelineStrength: Primary guideline anticoagulation recommendations include Class 1, level B-R for anticoagulation and DOAC preference in eligible patients; advanced-treatment classes vary.
title: 2026 AHA/ACC/ACCP/ACEP/CHEST/SCAI/SHM/SIR/SVM/SVN Guideline for the Evaluation and Management of Acute Pulmonary Embolism in Adults: A Report of the American College of Cardiology/American Heart Association Joint Committee on Clinical Practice Guidelines
shortTitle: 2026 PE guideline: severity categories connect risk to disposition
summary: The first AHA/ACC multisociety acute PE guideline introduces categories A–E to connect severity with outpatient care, admission and advanced therapy. It emphasizes prompt anticoagulation and prefers DOACs over vitamin K antagonists when appropriate.
whyItMatters: Use structured severity assessment for disposition and escalation, rather than clot size alone. Confirm outpatient treatment feasibility and arrange early follow-up; pregnancy requires a separate anticoagulant choice.
limitations: Many escalation decisions depend on bleeding risk, local expertise and evidence with variable certainty. The categories do not make every low-risk patient suitable for discharge or every high-risk patient suitable for intervention.
intervention: Risk classification, diagnostic, anticoagulation, disposition and advanced-treatment recommendations.
comparator: Prior practice without a unified AHA/ACC acute PE guideline.
primaryEndpoint: Guideline recommendations, not a single clinical-trial endpoint.
findings: Categories A/B often permit outpatient care; C–E require hospitalization according to the official society summary.
DOACs are preferred over vitamin K antagonists in eligible patients; DOACs are not recommended in pregnancy.
Higher-risk patients may need multidisciplinary assessment for reperfusion or other advanced support.
evidenceNotes: ACC official February 19 release reviewed; selected primary guideline anticoagulation tables cross-checked. Complete guideline not reviewed. The JACC co-publication has PMID 41712898 and DOI 10.1016/j.jacc.2025.11.005; do not create a second record for it.
